html:
A way of painting Greek pottery, invented in Athens around 530 BCE, in which the figures are left the reddish colour of the clay and the background is painted black. It reversed the earlier black-figure style.

Because the details were now drawn with a brush instead of scratched in, painters could show muscles, folds of cloth, faces turned in three-quarter view and bodies in motion. For a while some vases had black-figure on one side and red-figure on the other. Leading painters of the early years include Euphronios and Euthymides, who competed openly; one wrote on a vase that Euphronios never painted so well.

Red-figure vases show gods, heroes, athletes and scenes of the symposium, and they are a main source for what Greeks looked like and did. They were exported widely, many to Etruscan buyers in Italy. By about 300 BCE the style had faded in Athens, though workshops in southern Italy carried it on for a while.
sum: A way of painting Greek pottery, invented in Athens around 530 BCE, in which the figures are left the reddish colour of the clay and the background is painted black. It reversed the earlier black-figure style.
